A1.justification: Both PDFs fully support comparison of the same LZ penalty research. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. v2's Appendix A relocates sweep results from v1's main text rather than adding previously missing material.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original AIME and GPQA accuracy/repetition experiments and SGLang latency/throughput measurements.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the original benchmark experiments, penalty sweeps, and latency/throughput measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same simulated LZSS marginal-codelength penalty, logit update, and final piecewise formula. The reference-compressor definition corrections and new diagram do not establish a change to the proposed inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate AIME and GPQA using QwQ-32B and R1-Distill-14B, alongside the same Qwen-2.5 efficiency benchmarks. Moving the sweeps into Appendix A adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the no-penalty baseline, repetition penalty, and frequency penalty. The efficiency study still compares inference with and without LZ; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Both retain the 24k token limit, top-p 0.95, top-k 40, LZ strength 0.15, window 512, buffer 32, and penalty/temperature sweeps. Efficiency benchmark settings also match. Omitted caption details do not establish a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The same penalty-strength and temperature sensitivity sweeps and frequency-penalty degeneration example are retained. Appendix A redisplays existing analyses; no new ablation, robustness test, or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Both report averages and empirical standard deviations over five runs, with the same accuracy error bars. No seed information, uncertainty procedure, or statistical test is added or removed.

E6.justification: The three experimental graphics are identical across versions: v1 Figures 1–3 match v2 Figures 3, 4, and 2. Table 1 also retains every value, including throughput slowdowns of 0.55%, 0.14%, and 0.03%.

T1.justification: Definition 7 changes the matched expression from y^k to the explicit prefix y≤k. Definition 8 extends the partial-match branch from L > 1 to l ≥ 1, covering singleton matches. The prediction-compression proposition and subsequent penalty derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The core claims of repetition suppression without capability loss and negligible overhead remain. The abstract slightly broadens its quantitative baseline-failure statement from 'up to 4%' to 'up to 4% or more'; no new contribution is claimed.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit limitations concerning complexity and the distinction between algorithmic and practical determinism. It discusses caching or fixed seeds as alternatives and hardware nondeterminism as a remaining obstacle. Existing interpretations of repetition suppression and overhead are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an additional lz-penalty repository link alongside the SGLang fork. However, it removes the line-chart caption's explicit baseline strengths of 1.1 and 0.1 and the qualification that batching assumes constant buffer and lookback sizes. Other implementation settings remain.

R1.justification: The same 25 cited works and the positioning relative to sampling penalties, LZ compression, and prediction-compression duality are retained. Citation numbering and bibliography ordering change without substantive repositioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a Limitations paragraph, trims background and discussion prose, adopts numerical citations, and moves the detailed sweep description into Appendix A. Most exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the visual presentation: it adds the sampling-loop diagram as Figure 1, promotes the existing line charts to the main results display as Figure 2, and moves both heatmaps into Appendix A as Figures 3–4. The experimental graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new limitations clarify why greedy decoding does not guarantee practical determinism, while Figure 1 and the definition corrections improve explanation. All empirical evidence is retained. Removing explicit baseline strengths and the batching qualification slightly weakens reproducibility documentation, but the gains in clarity and qualification support a modest overall improvement.
